source_meta._title: Breaking a double resin brick slab block only returns a single slab

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4 in an unmodified single-player Survival world with commands allowed. Use the default doTileDrops gamerule and an unenchanted wooden pickaxe. No particular seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, or world type is required by the report.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4 is installed and selectable in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use a vanilla world without gameplay-modifying mods or datapacks so that the version's standard resin brick slab loot table is tested.
Create the test world in Survival mode with Allow Commands enabled; commands are used only to obtain the exact setup items without adding crafting or exploration.
Leave the doTileDrops gamerule at its default value of true so broken blocks can produce item drops.
Ensure there is room in the inventory for dropped items, and do not use a pickaxe enchanted with Silk Touch.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.4 and start the game.
steps.exact_input: Select Java Edition 1.21.4, then select Play.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition title screen is open and displays version 1.21.4.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Survival mode. In the world-creation settings, turn Allow Commands on, then create the world. No specific seed or other world-generation setting is required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Survival -> Allow Commands: On -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a Survival world and the health, hunger, and hotbar HUD are visible.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until the initial terrain has rendered and normal player movement and input respond without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, chunks are no longer visibly appearing around the player, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Obtain exactly two resin brick slabs. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly as shown with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and two Resin Brick Slab items are present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Obtain one ordinary, unenchanted wooden pickaxe. Press T, enter the command exactly as shown with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and an unenchanted Wooden Pickaxe is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Place the stack of two Resin Brick Slabs in hotbar slot 1, which is the far-left hotbar slot. Place the Wooden Pickaxe in hotbar slot 2. Close the inventory by pressing E again.
steps.exact_input: E; move 2 Resin Brick Slabs to hotbar slot 1; move the Wooden Pickaxe to hotbar slot 2; E
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains exactly two Resin Brick Slabs, hotbar slot 2 contains the Wooden Pickaxe, and the inventory screen is closed.

steps.action: Find the upward-facing surface of any solid full block, such as a grass block or stone block, with an empty block space immediately above it. Stand within placement reach, press 1 to select the Resin Brick Slabs, and aim the crosshair at the top face of the supporting block.
steps.success_cue: The Resin Brick Slabs are selected in the active hotbar slot, and the crosshair points at a clear top surface where the test slab can be placed.

steps.action: Right-click once on the top face of the supporting block to place the first resin brick slab as a lower slab in the empty space above the support.
steps.success_cue: One lower Resin Brick Slab occupies the bottom half of the block space above the support, and one Resin Brick Slab remains in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Keep the crosshair aimed at the upward-facing top surface of the placed resin brick slab. Right-click once more so the second slab merges with the first slab in the same block space. Do not aim at the side of the slab or at an adjacent block.
steps.success_cue: The two slabs have combined into a full-height double resin brick slab occupying one block space, rather than forming separate slabs in adjacent or vertically separate spaces. No Resin Brick Slab items remain in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Press 2 to select the unenchanted Wooden Pickaxe in the active hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The Wooden Pickaxe is visible in the player's hand and hotbar slot 2 is highlighted.

steps.action: Position the player far enough from the double slab that any resulting item entities are less likely to be collected immediately, while remaining within Survival-mode breaking reach. Aim the crosshair directly at the double resin brick slab, not at the supporting block.
steps.exact_input: Use normal movement controls, then center the crosshair on the double resin brick slab.
steps.success_cue: The double resin brick slab is targeted and outlined, the wooden pickaxe remains selected, and the player is within breaking reach without standing directly against the block.

steps.action: Hold left-click continuously until the targeted double resin brick slab finishes breaking. Release left-click immediately when the block disappears, and do not move toward or manually collect any resulting item entities.
steps.exact_input: Hold left-click until the double resin brick slab breaks, then release.
steps.success_cue: The double resin brick slab has just been removed from its block position, the breaking action is complete, and the player has not intentionally moved into the drop location.

stor.handoff_condition: The unenchanted wooden pickaxe has just finished breaking the double resin brick slab in Survival mode. The player has released left-click and has not moved toward or intentionally collected the resulting drops. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before performing any additional action.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode or item-acquisition method. This plan uses Survival mode because normal block drops must be produced, with commands enabled solely to obtain the setup items deterministically.
The report states that any pickaxe level can be used but does not name a material. An unenchanted wooden pickaxe is selected as the simplest representative of the stated condition.
The report provides no seed, coordinates, biome, support block, or world type. The plan therefore uses any accessible solid block with clear space above it.

The item-acquisition commands are operational additions and were not supplied by the report; they preserve the reported test state of placing exactly two resin brick slabs and breaking the resulting double slab with a pickaxe.

source_meta._title: Shulker boxes drop their contents when broken

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 25w02a, unmodified vanilla client, singleplayer world, Survival mode at the trigger, keyboard and mouse controls. Use a newly created world with commands enabled solely to acquire deterministic test items; no specific seed, coordinates, difficulty, dimension, datapack, resource pack, or server configuration is specified by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot 25w02a. Do not use fix version 25w03a or a newer version.
Use an unmodified vanilla instance without datapacks or mods that replace shulker box loot tables or container behavior.
Create or load a singleplayer world in which commands are enabled. The player must be in Survival mode before breaking the shulker box.
Ensure there is accessible solid ground with enough open space above it for a shulker box to open.
Ensure the player inventory has at least four free slots for one shulker box, one iron pickaxe, and two stacks of test contents.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft: Java Edition using the 25w02a installation and verify the version shown on the title screen before opening a world.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game version as 25w02a.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Set the game mode to Survival, enable commands or cheats, and create the world. The seed and other world-generation settings may remain at their defaults. Wait for terrain to render and for movement to respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded singleplayer world, movement responds normally, and the Survival health and hunger bars are visible.

steps.action: Open in-game chat and give the player one empty shulker box. Include the leading slash because this command is being entered through in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that one shulker box was given, and the shulker box is present in the player inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Open in-game chat and give the player one new, unenchanted iron pickaxe to serve as the proper mining tool.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that one iron pickaxe was given, and an iron pickaxe is present in the player inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Open in-game chat and give the player one stack of cobblestone as the first arbitrary item stack to store in the shulker box.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that 64 cobblestone were given, and the stack is present in the player inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Open in-game chat and give the player one stack of dirt as the second arbitrary item stack to store in the shulker box.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback reports that 64 dirt were given, and the stack is present in the player inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Locate the shulker box and iron pickaxe, then drag the shulker box into hotbar slot 1 and the iron pickaxe into hotbar slot 2. Leave the cobblestone and dirt anywhere in the player inventory. Press E or Esc to close the inventory.
steps.exact_input: E; drag Shulker Box to hotbar slot 1; drag Iron Pickaxe to hotbar slot 2; E or Esc
steps.success_cue: The closed inventory view shows the shulker box in hotbar slot 1 and the iron pickaxe in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Press 1 to select the shulker box in hotbar slot 1. Aim the crosshair at the top face of a nearby solid ground block with open space above it, then right-click once to place the shulker box.
steps.success_cue: A closed shulker box block is visible on the ground in front of the player.

steps.action: Keep the crosshair aimed at the placed shulker box and right-click it once to open its container interface.
steps.success_cue: The shulker box interface is open, showing an upper storage grid of 27 slots and the player inventory below it.

steps.action: In the open shulker box interface, locate the stack of 64 cobblestone in the lower player-inventory area. Hold Shift and left-click that stack once to transfer it into the shulker box storage grid.
steps.success_cue: A stack of 64 cobblestone is visible in one of the upper shulker box storage slots.

steps.action: Locate the stack of 64 dirt in the lower player-inventory area. Hold Shift and left-click that stack once to transfer it into the shulker box storage grid.
steps.success_cue: The upper shulker box storage grid contains both the cobblestone stack and the dirt stack.

steps.action: Press Esc to close the shulker box interface. Remain near the box and wait until its lid-closing animation has completely finished before continuing.
steps.success_cue: First-person world view is restored and the placed shulker box lid is visually fully closed.

steps.action: Explicitly set the player to Survival mode immediately before the mining test. Press T to open chat, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms Survival mode, and the health and hunger bars are visible above the hotbar.

steps.action: Press 2 to select the unenchanted iron pickaxe in hotbar slot 2. Aim the crosshair directly at the closed shulker box and stand close enough that its block outline appears when targeted.
steps.success_cue: The iron pickaxe is visible in the player's main hand and the closed, filled shulker box is targeted by the crosshair.

steps.action: Hold the left mouse button continuously to mine the targeted shulker box with the iron pickaxe. Release the button as soon as the block finishes breaking. Do not move toward or pick up any resulting item entities before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Hold left mouse button until the shulker box block breaks, then release
steps.success_cue: The shulker box block has completed its breaking action and no longer occupies its placed block position; the player has not moved to collect anything.

stor.handoff_condition: The closed, non-empty shulker box has just been mined to completion in Survival mode with an unenchanted iron pickaxe, and the player remains stationary before collecting any resulting item entities. Begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, dimension, difficulty, or multiplayer requirement; this plan uses a new singleplayer world and arbitrary accessible solid ground.

The report says to fill the box with random content but does not identify particular items or quantities. This plan deterministically uses one full stack of cobblestone and one full stack of dirt as arbitrary contents.

The report describes only a proper tool without naming it. A pickaxe was selected because shulker boxes are identified as pickaxe-mineable; the report does not require a particular pickaxe material or enchantment.

Commands and enabled cheats are not stated reproduction requirements. They are used only to acquire the test items deterministically while keeping the actual placement, filling, and breaking sequence in Survival mode.

No requirement is given to reproduce the separate piston or explosion duplication variant mentioned in a comment; this plan covers only the primary report procedure of manually mining the shulker box with a proper tool.

source_meta._title: Harvesting from sweet berry bushes can drop more sweet berries than before

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 25w32a in an unmodified single-player world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled. A flat, open area with solid ground is recommended so the relative /fill command can place and retain all 100 sweet berry bushes. Keyboard and mouse instructions refer to the default controls.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 25w32a, not the fixed snapshot 25w34a.
Use a world in which commands are permitted; Creative mode with cheats enabled is the simplest practical configuration.
Use an unmodified vanilla world with no datapack or mod that replaces the sweet berry bush harvesting loot table.
Stand on level, solid ground with at least a 10-by-10-block unobstructed area around the player.
Ensure the player's inventory contains no sweet berries before the first harvest so the quantity produced by one interaction can be isolated.
Have at least one empty hotbar slot and sufficient empty inventory space to collect the harvested berries.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start the Java Edition installation for snapshot 25w32a. If snapshots are hidden, enable snapshot versions in the launcher's installation/version controls before selecting it.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game version as 25w32a.

steps.action: Create a new disposable single-player world, selecting Creative mode and enabling commands/cheats in the world-creation settings. A flat world is preferred, but any world with a sufficiently large, level, solid surface is usable.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a 25w32a world in Creative mode and commands are available.

steps.action: Move to a level area and stand normally on a solid ground block. Confirm that the player's feet occupy air directly above the ground and that a 10-by-10 area beginning at the player's position and extending toward increasing X and increasing Z is unobstructed. In a flat world, any open location away from placed structures is sufficient.
steps.success_cue: There is solid ground directly below the intended bush layer and enough open space for a 10-by-10 square of bushes.

steps.action: Check that the inventory contains no sweet berries. Press E to open the inventory, inspect both the hotbar and main inventory, and select an empty hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E. If the inventory is not empty because this is not a fresh world, store existing sweet berries away from the test area before continuing.
steps.success_cue: No sweet berries are present in the player's inventory, and the active hotbar slot is empty so the player is not holding an item that could alter the interaction.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat and command entry field.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's /fill command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command places one horizontal 10-by-10 layer of sweet berry bushes at age 3, with the player's current block position as one corner.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds and a 10-by-10 square containing 100 fully grown sweet berry bushes is visible at the player's feet level.

steps.action: Move out of the bush square without right-clicking any bush. In Creative mode, double-tap Space to begin flying, rise above the bushes with Space, move laterally beyond one edge using the movement controls, and descend beside the square using the Sneak control, Left Shift by default. Do not left-click or break any bushes.
steps.exact_input: Space twice; movement keys as needed; Left Shift to descend
steps.success_cue: The player is positioned on or immediately above unobstructed ground beside the square, and all bushes remain at age 3 and unharvested.

steps.action: Keep the empty hotbar slot selected. Aim the crosshair at one age-3 bush on the outside edge of the square so it can be reached without walking through other bushes. Do not hold bone meal, sweet berries, or any other item.
steps.success_cue: A single fully grown edge bush is under the crosshair and within interaction range, while the player's inventory still contains no sweet berries.

steps.action: Use the bush exactly once by pressing and immediately releasing the Use Item/Place Block control, which is the right mouse button by default. Do not hold the button down, and do not interact with a second bush before the observation subsystem inspects this harvest.
steps.success_cue: The selected bush has changed from its fully grown age-3 state to its post-harvest growth state, and no other bush has been harvested.

stor.handoff_condition: One age-3 sweet berry bush has just been right-clicked exactly once while the player started with no sweet berries in the inventory. The clicked bush is now in its post-harvest state, all other bushes remain untouched, and no second interaction has occurred. Transfer control immediately so the observation subsystem can inspect and record the items produced by this individual harvest before another bush is used.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world type, or whether the reproduction must occur on a dedicated server. A fresh Creative-mode single-player world with cheats enabled is selected as the simplest environment that preserves the reported command and harvesting interaction.

The harvest quantity is randomized, so one individual interaction may not demonstrate every possible quantity. The 10-by-10 command supplies 100 separate bushes so additional trials can be performed on untouched bushes, one at a time, after each prior trial has been recorded and the player's sweet berry inventory has been reset.

The report does not prescribe how to isolate the quantity from one harvest. Beginning with no sweet berries and prohibiting a second interaction until the first is inspected is a practical measurement choice rather than an explicit report requirement.
